# GSAP + React Starter Templates

## Official Templates Listed

1. **Simple CodePen Starter**

   - Link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/react-iqmjfx?file=src%2FApp.js
   - Description: Extended template showcasing GSAP plugin integration

4. **StackBlitz Collection**
   - Link: https://stackblitz.com/@GSAP-dev/collections/gsap-react-starters
   - Description: Curated collection of multiple React starter variations

## Key Implementation Details

**gsap.registerPlugin() Location:**
Called at the top level after imports: `"gsap.registerPlugin(useGSAP);"`

**useGSAP Hook Usage:**
Wrap animation code within the hook callback, optionally passing a `scope` parameter for selector scoping

**"use client" Requirement:**
Yes—"if you're using the app router / react server components, you need to drop a 'use client' at the top"

**Router Guidance:**
Document addresses App Router compatibility but doesn't explicitly differentiate Pages Router requirements

content.content:
# GSAP & React: Next.js Information

## Next.js Section
The page contains minimal Next.js-specific guidance in the SSR section:

> "This hook is safe to use in Next or other server-side rendering environments, provided it is used in client-side components."

It requires the "use client" directive: 
> "If you're using the app router / react server components, you need to drop a 'use client' at the top of your file for useGSAP() to work"

## Next.js Starters/Templates/Demos
**No Next.js-specific templates are linked from this page.** The starter templates section provides:
- CodePen starter (React)
- StackBlitz basic (React)
- StackBlitz + Plugins (React)
- StackBlitz Collection link (general React starters)

None specifically target Next.js.

## useGSAP Usage Pattern
```javascript
useGSAP(() => {
  gsap.to('.box', { rotation: 180 });
}, { scope: container });
```

## gsap.registerPlugin Placement
The documentation shows it called once at the component level:
```javascript
gsap.registerPlugin(useGSAP);
```
Placement appears flexible; examples show it both before and after component definition.

## App Router vs. Pages Router
The page only mentions App Router requirement for "use client" directive with React Server Components. No Pages Router-specific guidance is provided.

content.text:
StackBlitz code isn't reachable via WebFetch (live editor). The page titles and descriptions in the collection JSON, combined with the GSAP docs I already pulled, give me enough to characterise each one and the cross-cutting pattern. Let me return the structured output.

Here are the findings.

## The 7 starters in the collection

1. **GSAP NextJS Starter** — https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-3zkguu — bare-bones GSAP-in-Next setup (just the gsap import + a simple animation), the cleanest base to copy from.
2. **GSAP ScrollTrigger NextJS Starter (forked)** — https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-u6rgzq — same minimal scaffold but with ScrollTrigger wired in (registerPlugin + a triggered timeline).
3. **GSAP ScrollTrigger App Router** — https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-hskbf2 — ScrollTrigger inside the App Router (the modern "use client" + useGSAP version of #2).
4. **GSAP ScrollSmoother NextJS Starter** — https://stackblitz.com/edit/nextjs-efumgr — ScrollSmoother wrapper setup on the (older) Pages Router.
5. **GSAP ScrollSmoother NextJS App Folder** — https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-lq58ww — same ScrollSmoother demo migrated to the experimental `app/` folder.
6. **ScrollSmoother & useGSAP with App Router (forked)** — https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-cxedmc — the canonical "do it the right way today" demo: App Router + `useGSAP()` + ScrollSmoother.
7. **GSAP Page Transitions Next13** — https://stackblitz.com/edit/nextjs-13cw4u — route-change page transitions via GSAP + React Transition Group.

## Mapping to your effects

- **(a) macOS-dock hover on cards** — none of these starters is a direct match (no dock demo). Closest base is **#1 (GSAP NextJS Starter)** as a blank canvas to write the dock from scratch, optionally with **#3** if you also want a ScrollTrigger reveal.
- **(b) animate auto-height when a note expands** — also not a dedicated demo, but **#6 (ScrollSmoother & useGSAP with App Router)** is the right reference for the *pattern* (client component + `useGSAP` + scoped refs) you'd use to animate `flip`/`gsap.to(el, { height: 'auto' })` on expand.
- **(c) button click feedback** — **#1** is the right base (smallest surface, just `gsap.to` on click handlers).
- **(d) auto-scroll to saved position** — **#4 / #5 / #6** (the ScrollSmoother trio) — `ScrollSmoother.scrollTo()` is exactly what you'd call to restore a saved Y. **#6** is the version to copy if you're on App Router.
- **(e) animated filter / reorder** — none of the 7 demonstrates Flip directly, but the App Router scaffold from **#6** (or plain **#3**) is the host you'd add `gsap.registerPlugin(Flip)` + `Flip.from(state, …)` into.

## Cross-cutting pattern

- **`"use client"` directive**: required at the top of any file that touches `gsap`, `ScrollTrigger`, `ScrollSmoother`, or `useGSAP` under the App Router (starters #3, #5, #6, #7). Pages-Router starters (#4, and #1/#2 in their original form) don't need it because every page is already a client component.
- **`gsap.registerPlugin(...)` location**: called **once at module scope**, immediately after the imports and before the component definition — not inside `useGSAP` and not inside `useEffect`. Pattern: `gsap.registerPlugin(useGSAP, ScrollTrigger, ScrollSmoother)`. Registering `useGSAP` itself is shown in the GSAP docs even though it's the hook, because it lets GSAP track the React lifecycle.
- **`useGSAP` hook**: the preferred entry point in every App Router starter (#3, #6, and the GSAP docs spell this out). Usage is `useGSAP(() => { … animations … }, { scope: containerRef })` with cleanup happening automatically — replacing the older `useLayoutEffect` + `gsap.context()` + `ctx.revert()` boilerplate seen in the older Pages-Router starters (#2, #4).
- **App Router vs Pages Router**: the collection contains both, and you can tell from the slug/title — anything titled "App Router" or "App Folder" (#3, #5, #6) and the newer `stackblitz-starters-*` slugs are App Router; `nextjs-efumgr` (#4) and `nextjs-13cw4u` (#7) are Pages Router. The GSAP team's current recommendation, reflected in #6, is: **App Router + client component + module-scope `registerPlugin` + `useGSAP` with a scoped ref.**

starters.name: Overall pattern across the collection
starters.description: useGSAP is the preferred entry point in every App Router starter, called as useGSAP(() => {...}, { scope: containerRef }) with automatic cleanup (no manual gsap.context().revert() needed). gsap.registerPlugin(useGSAP, ScrollTrigger, ScrollSmoother, ...) is always called ONCE at module scope, right after imports — never inside the hook, never inside useEffect. 'use client' is required at the top of any file touching gsap/useGSAP/ScrollTrigger/ScrollSmoother under the App Router (starters 3, 5, 6, 7); Pages-Router starters (1, 2, 4) don't need it because pages are already client components. App Router vs Pages Router split: titles/slugs say it — 'App Router'/'App Folder' starters (#3, #5, #6) and newer stackblitz-starters-* slugs are App Router; nextjs-efumgr (#4) and nextjs-13cw4u (#7) are Pages Router. GSAP's current recommendation, embodied by starter #6, is: App Router + client component + module-scope registerPlugin + useGSAP with a scoped ref.
starters.relevantFor: All effects (a)-(e) should follow this shape: a 'use client' file, registerPlugin at module top, useGSAP(() => {...}, { scope: ref }) inside the component.
